newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Qantas says first qtr on track.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Qantas says first qtr on track.

text.p: MELBOURNE, Nov 20 - Qantas Airways Ltd, which earlier forecast that an improvement in 1996/97 earnings would depend on a stronger final six months, said its first quarter trading performance was in line with the full year analysis.

"It was at a level that supported the view that I have given for the full year outlook," chairman Gary Pemberton told reporters when asked about trading in the first three months to September 30. He did not reveal specific figures.
Asked if the quarterly result was in line with budget, Pemberton said: "Budget is a bit of a moving feast when the market is softening."
Pemberton also repeated at a news conference after the annual meeting that he believed 1996/97 profits would rise.
"We are confident that we will be able to deliver improved profit (in the full year) but the actual margin on that will be comparatively sensitive to the second half."
In his speech, Pemberton said higher fuel costs and the stronger Australian dollar would have a negative impact on earnings with any full year improvement to depend on second half market conditions.
Qantas, which is 25 percent owned by British Airways Plc, achieved a 37 percent rise in 1995/96 net profit to A$146.2 million.
